INT-002: You want to work with an agent the vibe-coding way, without micro-managing it and without heavy spec-driven ceremony, while every turn stays grounded in the project's own artifacts, cheaply, reliably and in a way you can trust.
INT-002 will: Give the agent the relevant records and tests as short context every turn.; Keep per-turn overhead to seconds.; Base trust on evidence: hashes, pinned approvals and pinned test evidence.
INT-002 won't: Micro-manage the agent through procedures.; Require a full up-front spec for ordinary work.
INT-002/A-1 assumption: Context naming which records and tests apply works better than procedure (TDAD).
items.owner_words: I find that the main issue with current coding agents is that we either have to micro manage them or 'vibe code / Spec driven develop' the thing. I'd like coherence to make vibe coding grounded on the projects artifacts in an efficient, reliable and trustable manner.

items.record_text:
INT-003: pi-agent-factory's governed workflows are too heavy and black-boxed. plumb should be a lighter, more elegant and interactive way to get the same alignment, working with the agent rather than driving it.
INT-003 will: Work through a few cheap hooks, a status line and a short summary.; Keep every piece of state inspectable as Markdown and JSON in git.
INT-003 won't: A run state machine, consent phrases, manifests, handoff hashes or review swarms.; Governed execution as the default way of working.
INT-003/A-1 assumption: Edits are tracked without ever blocking the agent's work.
items.owner_words: they seem pretty heavy, and also quite orthogonal to the developments claude and other coding agents are doing ... whether that really makes sense to have those heavy blackboxed workflows in the first place. isnt there a more elegant way of doing things nowadays? ... a lighter, more elegant and interactive way to leverage coherence.

items.record_text:
INT-004: Planning stays, in mode C: intent is captured incrementally by default, and large, risky or cross-cutting work escalates to an explicit up-front spec you approve. The same records serve both modes and plumb suggests when to escalate. Your intent is translated through a read-back in your terms, examples you confirm, decisions made explicit, traceable links and drift signals.
INT-004 will: Read back what will and won't be done, with assumptions labelled.; Anchor requirements in given/when/then examples that become tests.; Make ambiguity an explicit decision (I assumed A; B also fits).; Link intent to requirement to examples and tests to code.; Suggest escalation to an up-front spec for large or risky work.
INT-004 won't: Block work on a proposed read-back or example (R1).
INT-004/A-1 assumption: Every requirement touched by a change is confirmed at the merge boundary (R1).

items.record_text:
INT-024: The agent, with plumb, is how you interact with the system you are designing and building: you work through the agent rather than with plumb or the code directly. So the agent needs the tools to present the right context about that system to you as well as possible, at your level, when it matters. A status line and an end-of-turn summary (INT-008) are not enough on their own.
INT-024 will: Give the agent the plumb tools it needs to present the system under design (your intent, its state, what awaits you) in your terms, whenever it is useful.; Treat INT-008's status line and short summary as part of this, not the whole of it.
INT-024 won't: Expect you to run plumb commands or read plumb files yourself to understand where the system under design stands.
INT-024/A-1 assumption: INT-023 (band, panel, summary line, Confirm buttons, speaking at your level) is the current plan for these tools; this intent is the goal they serve.
INT-024/A-2 assumption: Which tools are missing is worked out in a later request, not decided here.
items.owner_words: I guess my intent is that the agent and plumb is the interface for the User to interact with the system. So the agent should have the required tools to present context as best as possible.
items.source: The owner stated this intent on 7 Oct (prompt 0524160b166ba1e2) and confirmed INT-024 at this hash (approval 2026-10-07T23:34:11Z, relayed).

items.record_text:
INT-028: You approve or reject the way you would talk to a person. A language model reads your whole message and the records you were shown, and says for each one whether you accepted it, rejected it, asked for a change, or left it open; no fixed words, no splitting your message into pieces, no hunting for objection words. Or you press an Accept or Reject button. plumb's own checks stay only where they are reliable: the message really came from you (the prompt hook logged it), the record was shown to you in full, and an unclear reading confirms nothing and asks you once.
INT-028 will: A language model extracts, from your logged message, your answer to each record you were shown: accepted, rejected (and whether the read-back misread you), change asked, or open; with the words that carry it.; plumb records that reading with your exact message, so it can be checked and undone.; Accept and Reject buttons for each shown record in a Claude Code window (SP7's panel), recording exactly what was shown.; Show a record in full before asking you about it, so your answer can settle it.; If no model can be reached, say so as an error you see, and confirm nothing; there is no fallback to word-based rules (your answer of 9 Oct: no labelled fallback, throw an error).
INT-028 won't: Parse your message with fixed rules as the main way of understanding it.; Let the coding agent decide, on its own reading, that you approved something.; Treat silence, or an unclear reading, as an approval.
INT-028/A-1 assumption: The reading comes from a model independent of the coding agent, called by plumb's prompt hook, so the agent cannot shape it.
INT-028/A-2 assumption: Buttons come from SP7's panel (SR-086).
items.owner_words: Then, this whole approval workflow should not rely on specific wording but understand user's approval or denial directly from the prompt semantic or through the mods UI buttons.
items.source: The owner stated this intent on 8 Oct (prompt f222cab629db17a4) and confirmed INT-028 at this hash with "1A 2B 3A  INT-028 and INT-029 ok" (approval 2026-10-09T22:23:45Z, relayed).

items.record_text:
INT-029: Wherever plumb has to understand what you mean (your intent, your answers, your corrections, the meaning of a record), it uses a language model, not fixed rules such as keyword lists, regular expressions or sentence splitting. Fixed rules stay only where they are provably complete for every case: hashes, file paths, record IDs, whether a message was logged, whether a record was shown.
INT-029 will: Use a language model for every step that interprets your words or a record's meaning.; Keep deterministic code for checks that are exact by nature (provenance, hashes, IDs, links, test results).; Remove today's word-based rules (affirmation words, objection words, plain-words matching) as the model-based reading lands, with no fallback to them.
INT-029 won't: Add more keyword or sentence-splitting rules to understand your messages.
INT-029/A-1 assumption: A model's reading is logged with your exact words and can be checked and undone, so it is never a hidden decision.
INT-029/A-2 assumption: When no model is reachable, plumb shows an error and confirms nothing; it does not fall back to rules.
items.owner_words: My intent is that most of the time the system shouldn't rely on deterministic tooling to understand intent or process text, unless we're sure the deterministic solution can handle any type of situation.
items.source: The owner stated this intent on 9 Oct (prompt 03becf60e75af185) and confirmed INT-029 at this hash with "INT-028 and INT-029 ok" (approval 2026-10-09T22:23:45Z, relayed).

INT-016/A-1 assumption: A record's line comes again after /clear or a compaction, since the agent lost it.

items.record_text:
INT-008: plumb works mostly in the background: a status-line indicator, a short alignment summary at the end of each turn, and a question only on a real intent change, an unconfirmed decision that matters, or a regression. Everything else is logged for you to read when you want.
INT-008 will: Show a status line and a short end-of-turn summary.; Ask only on an intent change, an unconfirmed decision that matters, or a regression.; Log everything else for on-demand reading.
INT-008 won't: Interrupt for a new test that starts red (R3).
INT-008/A-1 assumption: A regression is a test that previously passed with recorded evidence and now fails (R3).
items.owner_words: A (answering: How much should the tool interrupt you during normal work? A. Mostly in the background (recommended): a status-line indicator shows alignment (the active intent, any stale links, the covering tests); a short alignment summary appears at the end of each turn; it only asks you something on a real change in intent, an unconfirmed decision that matters, or a regression; everything else is logged for you to read whenever you want. B. A checkpoint every turn you approve before the next one. C. Only when asked: silent unless you run a command.)
